title: Tolan: Voice-First AI Companion — Paula Dozsa, Tolan
talk_summary: Tolan is a voice-first AI companion app whose engineers describe routing turns across a tiered model fleet by stakes, rebuilding context every turn instead of reusing it, and running a fleet of coding agents (implementation, review, PR shepherd, triage) wired via MCP into Linear/Sentry/Datadog. They also describe an eval-driven character build using multiple judge agents and find-fix-verify rounds against production logs.

takeaways.technique: Stakes-based tiered routing with a cheap classifier
takeaways.what_they_do: A small cheap-model 'tone router' classifies every turn; high-stakes turns (first message, onboarding, emotionally serious) always go to the frontier model, light turns and all background work go to small models. They route on stakes, not cost.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we route based on stakes not on cost. So the high stakes moments always get the best model.
takeaways.numbers: frontier model costs ~5x the smaller one; routing a third of turns to the small model had almost no measurable effect on retention

takeaways.technique: Rebuild context per turn instead of reusing it
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue reused context is actively wrong once the user pivots.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every turn we reassemble the context window from parts

takeaways.technique: PR shepherd agent that iterates to green
takeaways.what_they_do: A dedicated agent watches an open PR and keeps iterating against CI failures and review comments until clean, separate from implementation and review agents.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have a PR shepherd that watches an open pull request and keeps iterating against CI failures and review comments until it's clean

takeaways.technique: Multiple review agents with distinct lenses before human
takeaways.what_they_do: Separate review agents enforce standards, and multiple model instances review each other before a human looks; for the character build, five judges attacked from different angles (fidelity, mechanics, code standards, skeptical-user ears, safety).
takeaways.evidence_quote: multiple Claudes basically review each other before a human looks

takeaways.technique: Find-fix-verify rounds against production logs with judge agents
takeaways.what_they_do: Agents mapped every behavior-bearing surface, wrote a spec ('voice Bible'), then five judges evaluated changes against real production logs over three find-fix-verify rounds before shipping.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they evaluated the changes against real production logs over three find fix verify rounds
takeaways.numbers: 7M tokens, 4.5 hours compute; ~2 weeks of work in an afternoon

takeaways.technique: Triage bot wired via MCP into issue/observability tools
takeaways.what_they_do: A triage bot fires on every inbound bug report and, via MCP connections to Linear, Sentry, Datadog, reconstructs the crash, routes it, and often opens the fixing PR itself.
